info.name: Tolerant publication E2E
info.description:
Verifies tolerant publication: a version whose documents fail to build is still published in draft
status, is marked with hasErrors, exposes per-document error details through the notification
endpoints, and is barred from every composition that would spread the error.

Endpoints under test:
  GET   /api/v2/packages/{packageId}/versions/{version}/notifications
  GET   /api/v2/packages/{packageId}/versions/{version}/changes/notifications
  GET   /api/v2/packages/{packageId}/versions/{version}/changes/summary    (hasErrors)
  GET   /api/v3/packages/{packageId}/versions/{version}          (hasErrors, contract summaries)
  GET   /api/v3/packages/{packageId}/versions                    (hasErrors)
  GET   /api/v2/packages/{packageId}/versions/{version}/documents (hasErrors)
  POST  /api/v2/packages/{packageId}/publish                     (release and baseline refusals)
  PATCH /api/v2/packages/{packageId}/versions/{version}          (status change refusal)

Auth: the api-key header carries a sysadm token; set apiKey to zeroDayConfiguration.accessToken
of the running instance.

Prerequisites: the backend and a tolerant-publication-capable build-task-consumer must be running.

Run from the repository root so the multipart fixtures resolve:
  newman run tests/api/tolerant_publication.postman_collection.json --working-dir . \
    --env-var baseUrl=http://localhost:8090 --env-var apiKey=<token>

Folder 02 uses a mixed fixture: one version with two API types (rest, asyncapi) and two contract
types (ddl, mcp over two endpoints), where three of its seven documents fail. It is there so the
per-type roll-ups are checked for discrimination, not just for being set.

Folder 09 checks that the two error flags stay apart: hasErrors describes the version's content and
changelogHasErrors describes its changelog, and neither reports the other's problem. It also checks
that the versions list and the version itself answer identically. A changelog that genuinely fails is
not constructible from source fixtures - every comparison-phase Error is an internal resolution
failure - so that half is covered by unit tests instead.

A unique suffix is generated once per run, so the collection is safe to re-run. Package aliases
stay within the API's 10-character limit.

01 - Tolerant draft publication
Publish broken document as draft

exec: pm.test('Broken draft publish accepted', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(202); });

item.name: Wait for broken draft

exec: pm.test('Wait for broken draft status endpoint succeeds', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });
pm.test('Wait for broken draft completes before timeout', function () { pm.expect.fail('publish timeout'); });
pm.test('Wait for broken draft ends with status \'complete\'', function () { pm.expect(json.status, json.message || '').to.eql('complete'); });
pm.test('Build result reports errors', function () { pm.expect(json.hasErrors).to.eql(true); });
pm.test('Build result reports no changelog errors', function () { pm.expect(json.changelogHasErrors).to.eql(false); });
